mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the economy, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where housing starts increase over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve due to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 2-month period signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth slows and corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where industrial production declines by more than 1% over a 2-month period.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 7%, it signals strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS grows by more than 1% MoM and UNRATE is below 7%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a single month, coupled with a CPI (CPIAUCSL) increase of less than 0.2%, signals strong labor demand without significant inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and CPIAUCSL increases by less than 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over a 6-month period signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as financial conditions ease and investment increases.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate decreases over a 6-month period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 2% over a 3-month period and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals strong supply-side growth with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 2% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 2% over 3 months and FEDFUNDS is below 2%.
